alert_pattern: [FIRING:1] <cluster> : KubePersistentVolumeFillingUp - PVC <name> in <cluster> is only N% free
environment: any k8s cluster (seen on transcode scratch storage)
diagnosis_steps: Extract PVC name and namespace from alert (alert body includes 'PVC <name> filling up in <cluster>' and % free)
Confirm current usage on the storage dashboard; post the panel screenshot showing % free
Check whether the writer is a transcode/scratch workload - these fill during big jobs and MAY self-recover when the job completes
Check the runbook link embedded in the alert (Runbook: KubePersistentVolumeFillingUp - Resizing PVCs)
resolution_steps: Resize the PVC upward (observed: +50GB on a volume at ~8% free), per the resizing-PVCs runbook
Verify free space recovers (observed: 8% -> 39% free after adding 50GB)
Post the after screenshot in thread; resolved
gotchas: PVCs only grow, never shrink - size increases are permanent cost
Ack the VictorOps incident early so it doesn't escalate while you work
escalation: App owner if the same PVC needs resizing repeatedly (indicates a leak/retention problem, not capacity)

alert_pattern: [FIRING:N] <cluster> : KubePodsNotReady (often N in the tens; engine pods)
environment: any aiWARE k8s cluster; usually engine pods
diagnosis_steps: List not-ready pods and bucket by state: kubectl get pods -n aiware | grep -vE 'Running|Completed' - states seen: ImagePullBackOff, CrashLoopBackOff, Error, Pending/Init

ImagePullBackOff: verify the image tag actually exists in the registry (docker manifest inspect <image>); also check engine BUILD state - builds not in 'Deployed' state have caused pulls of unavailable images
Pending with FailedScheduling: read the event - node taints observed (ToBeDeletedByClusterAutoscaler, uninitialized, network-unavailable) usually mean node churn in progress
Error/CrashLoop: grep pod logs for the failure signature: panic|fatal|context deadline|Throttl|OOM|connection refused
Common crash signature: engine toolkit 'Failed to start subprocess [/opt/runner] err=context deadline exceeded' = engine couldn't reach the edge controller at startup
Check node health for the affected pods (kubectl describe node - pressure conditions, Ready history)
Check whether an ongoing change (cluster upgrade, controller rollout, load test) explains it - link the change thread
resolution_steps: Bulk-delete pods stuck in Error so the controller recreates them (observed 3500+ Error pods deleted at once)
If new pods immediately re-enter Error with the same log signature, deleting is futile - the dependency (edge controller / registry) is the problem; fix that first
For engine builds not Deployed: deploy the builds, pods recover
For autoscaler taint churn: usually self-heals as nodes finish cycling; monitor
Confirm backlogs drain after pods recover; resolved
gotchas: FIRING count is inflated - 50 crashlooping pods is usually ONE root cause (one engine build, one dependency, one node event)
If controller pods were rolled after the incident window, the relevant logs are gone - note it and move on rather than guessing
Deleting Error pods without checking the crash signature just burns scheduler cycles when the root cause persists
escalation: Engine/platform team when the crash is inside engine code or builds need redeployment
example_commands: kubectl get pods -n aiware --no-headers | grep eng | awk '{count[$3]++} END {for (s in count) print s, count[s]}'
